name: Cartagena
summary: Explore the walled city and Getsemaní around the heat of the day. Treat island outings as booked excursions with explicit inclusions and weather contingencies.
seasonNote: Dry-season months are popular; heat and humidity persist year-round.
arrival: CTG is close to the old city; use an authorized airport taxi or booked transfer.
gettingAround: Walk compact historic districts; use arranged transport for distant sights and the port.
cashTip: Carry small peso notes; agree prices before ordering on beaches or taking informal services.
foodTip: Try arepas, coconut rice, fried fish or vegetable dishes; agree complete meal prices.
buyTip: Look for Colombian coffee, woven bags and craft; verify materials and avoid wildlife products.
baseArea: Walled city or Getsemaní, according to noise tolerance.

connections.note: Indicative connecting journey; check actual schedules.
Approximate air time if direct service operates.

reviewSummary: The walled city has an indexed 4.7/5 snapshot from 23,367 reviews; San Felipe fort shows 4.4/5 from 13,278. Both support a history-led first day.

items.name: Walled City & sunset ramparts
items.summary: Walk colourful streets and sections of the Caribbean-facing walls.
items.expect: Busy streets and strong heat; some ramparts have uneven edges.
items.tip: Explore early, rest midday and return for sunset.
items.priceNote: Public streets and accessible wall walks free.

review.note: Indexed visitor-rating snapshot; check live reviews for changes.

whyVisit: The walls and streets make Cartagena’s fortified coastal history visible on foot.
A return in evening light changes both the temperature and the Caribbean view.
visitFlow: Walk a shaded street route early.
Return to an open rampart section for sunset.
items.bestFor: A first visit to the colonial city
items.tradeoffs: Busy streets and strong heat; some ramparts have uneven edges.

items.name: Castillo San Felipe de Barajas
items.summary: A massive defensive fort with tunnels and city views.
items.expect: Steep exposed ramps and hot stone surfaces.
items.tip: Bring water and start early; a guide helps explain the defence system.
items.priceNote: Planning estimate per adult; check the current official price.

review.note: Indexed visitor-rating snapshot; check live reviews for changes.

whyVisit: Massive defensive forms and tunnels reveal how the port was protected.
The fort’s elevation provides a view over surrounding Cartagena.
visitFlow: Begin early with water and a map or guide.
Follow the permitted ramps and tunnels before pausing at the viewpoints.
items.tradeoffs: Steep exposed ramps and hot stone surfaces.

items.name: Getsemaní street-art walk
items.summary: Murals and small squares create a different atmosphere from the grand old centre.
items.expect: Residential streets with growing nightlife and visitor traffic.
items.tip: Respect homes, ask before portraits and keep noise down.

review.note: Exact attraction listing snapshot; review volume is not visitor count.

whyVisit: Murals and smaller squares give a different scale from the grand walled centre.
The neighbourhood’s living streets make respectful observation more rewarding than a photo-only stop.
visitFlow: Follow a daylight mural route.
Pause in a public square and support a local food or craft business.
items.tradeoffs: Residential streets with growing nightlife and visitor traffic.

items.name: Rosario Islands day trip
items.summary: A boat excursion swaps the city for Caribbean islands and swimming.
items.expect: A full day with sea-state exposure; beach quality and crowding vary by operator.
items.tip: Confirm port fees, lunch, drinks, beach access and return time in writing.
items.priceNote: Planning estimate for shared day excursion; compulsory fees and premium beach clubs vary.

review.note: Included in the researched destination shortlist; no verified numeric rating snapshot. Open current visitor reviews.

whyVisit: Island waters and beaches provide a clear landscape contrast to the hot city.
A well-chosen operator can combine time afloat with a deliberate island base.
visitFlow: Confirm the exact island, beach access and all inclusions.
Follow the boat itinerary and leave a buffer for the return crossing.
items.tradeoffs: A full day with sea-state exposure; beach quality and crowding vary by operator.

items.summary: Combine a hilltop convent visit with an overview of Cartagena and its bay.
items.expect: A hilltop attraction outside the walled-city walking circuit.
items.tip: Arrange the return ride; do not treat the approach as a routine pedestrian route.
items.priceNote: Planning estimate in local currency; confirm the current price and what is included.

review.note: Exact attraction listing snapshot; review volume is not visitor count.

whyVisit: The elevated position gives a broad city-and-coast panorama.

visitFlow: Arrange a return taxi or guided transfer to the hilltop.

items.tradeoffs: Transport and admission are separate; midday heat can be intense.

dayClusters.label: The walled city at a comfortable pace
dayClusters.note: Walk early, use the church/museum or a long lunch during the heat, and browse the northern arcades. Return to the walls near sunset if desired; the group is within the old city.

dayClusters.label: San Felipe and Getsemani
dayClusters.note: Start the exposed fort early, then take a short transfer or appropriate daylight walk to Getsemani for food and neighbourhood exploration. Rest during the hottest hours.

dayClusters.label: Rosario Islands boat day
dayClusters.note: Reserve the whole day, including port formalities and the return sailing. Weather can change or cancel the trip; confirm all port, meal and beach-access charges.
